items.answer: (iv) 98.6 °F Use the conversion formula °F = (9/5 × °C) + 32. For 37 °C, 9 / 5 × 37 = 66.6

items.stem: Fill in the blanks: (i) The hotness or coldness of a system is determined by its __________. (ii) The temperature of ice-cold water cannot be measured by a __________ thermometer. (iii) The unit of temperature is degree __________.
items.answer: (i) Temperature (ii) Clinical (iii) Celsius

items.stem: The range of a laboratory thermometer is usually __________. (i) 10 °C to 100 °C (ii) –10 °C to 110 °C (iii) 32 °C to 45 °C (iv) 35 °C to 42 °C
items.answer: (ii) –10 °C to 110 °C A laboratory thermometer must cover temperatures below freezing and above boiling for common experiments, so its scale is typically extended from –10 °C up to 110 °C.

items.stem: Four students used a laboratory thermometer to measure the temperature of water as shown in Figure. Who do you think followed the correct way for measuring temperature? (i) Student 1 (ii) Student 2 (iii) Student 3 (iv) Student 4
items.answer: (ii) Student 2 Student 2’s method is correct because the thermometer bulb is fully immersed in the water without touching the vessel, the stem is held upright, and the reading is taken with the eye level at the liquid column. This avoids parallax error and ensures the bulb is actually sensing the water’s temperature, not the surrounding air or the beaker wall.

items.stem: A laboratory thermometer is not used to measure our body temperature. Give a reason.
items.answer: A laboratory thermometer is not meant for the body because it must stay upright and dipped in a liquid while you read it, and its wide scale (−10 °C to 110 °C) is too broad for the narrow human- temperature range. A clinical thermometer, with a 35 °C – 42 °C scale and a constriction that locks the reading, is made specially for measuring body temperature.

items.stem: If you have to measure the temperature 22.5 °C, which of the following three thermometers will you use (Figure)? Explain.
items.answer: Use the laboratory thermometer that has 0.5 °C divisions and a scale extending well below and above 22 °C (often marked –10 °C to 110 °C). It alone can (i) show 22 °C on its scale and (ii) let you read the extra half-division to reach 22.5 °C. The clinical thermometer is unsuitable because its range starts near 35 °C, and a laboratory thermometer with 1 °C divisions cannot show the half-degree value accurately.

items.stem: The temperature shown by the thermometer in figure is (i) 28.0 °C (ii) 27.5 °C (iii) 26.5 °C (iv) 25.3 °C
items.answer: (ii) 27.5 °C The mercury column ends exactly halfway between the 27 °C and 28 °C marks. Each small division on this thermometer represents 0.5 °C, so the halfway point is 27 °C + 0.5 °C = 27.5 °C, matching option (ii).

items.stem: A laboratory thermometer has 50 divisions between 0 °C and 100 °C. What does each division of this thermometer measure?
items.answer: Each division measures 2 °C (because 100 °C ÷ 50 divisions = 2 °C per division).

items.stem: Komal tells you that she has a fever of 101 degrees. Does she mean it on the Celsius scale or Fahrenheit scale?
items.answer: She must be talking about 101 °F. A body temperature of 101 °C would boil water and is impossible; doctors use the Fahrenheit scale when they say someone has a fever of 101 degrees.

items.stem: What is temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: The amount of heat energy contained in a body

options.label: B
options.text: A reliable measure of the hotness or coldness of a body

options.label: C
options.text: The flow of energy from a hotter body to a colder body

options.label: D
options.text: The feeling of warmth or coldness on touching an object

items.answer: (B) A reliable measure of the hotness or coldness of a body. Temperature is defined as a reliable and quantifiable measure that indicates how hot or cold an object or a body is. It helps in comparing the degree of hotness between different bodies.

items.stem: What did Phiban use to confirm if Lambok had a fever?

options.label: A
options.text: Her hand to touch his forehead

options.label: B
options.text: A wet cloth

options.label: C
options.text: A thermometer

options.label: D
options.text: A traditional herbal remedy

items.answer: (C) A thermometer. After feeling Lambok’s forehead, Phiban used a thermometer kept in the almirah to measure his temperature accurately and confirm whether he had a fever.

items.stem: Why can our sense of touch sometimes be misleading in judging whether a body is hot or cold, as demonstrated in Activity 7.1?

options.label: A
options.text: Because our hands are always at a constant temperature

options.label: B
options.text: Because the temperature of objects changes rapidly upon touch

options.label: C
options.text: Because the sensation of hotness or coldness is relative to the previous exposure of our hand

options.label: D
options.text: Because some materials do not conduct heat well

items.answer: (C) Because the sensation of hotness or coldness is relative to the previous exposure of our hand. The same water can feel cool to a hand previously in warm water and warm to a hand previously in cold water. This demonstrates that our sense of touch is relative and not always reliable.

items.stem: What is a thermometer?

options.label: A
options.text: A device used to measure the heat content of a body

options.label: B
options.text: A device that measures temperature

options.label: C
options.text: An instrument to observe changes in weather

options.label: D
options.text: A scale used to compare the sizes of objects

items.answer: (B) A device that measures temperature. A thermometer is an instrument specifically designed and calibrated to measure the temperature of a substance or a body accurately.

items.stem: What type of thermometer is generally used for measuring human body temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: Laboratory thermometer

options.label: B
options.text: Weather thermometer

options.label: C
options.text: Clinical thermometer

options.label: D
options.text: Infrared thermometer for industrial use

items.answer: (C) Clinical thermometer Clinical thermometers are specifically designed for measuring human body temperatures and typically have a temperature range suitable for this purpose. Digital clinical thermometers are commonly used.

items.stem: What is the primary advantage of digital clinical thermometers over traditional mercury thermometers?

options.label: A
options.text: Digital thermometers are less expensive

options.label: B
options.text: Digital thermometers measure temperature more slowly

options.label: C
options.text: Digital thermometers pose no risk of mercury poisoning if broken and are easier to read

options.label: D
options.text: Mercury thermometers can measure a wider range of temperatures

items.answer: (C) Digital thermometers pose no risk of mercury poisoning if broken and are easier to read. Mercury is a toxic substance. Digital thermometers eliminate this risk, and their digital display makes temperature readings clearer and easier to interpret compared to mercury thermometers.

items.stem: What is the unit of temperature on the Celsius scale?

options.label: A
options.text: Degree Fahrenheit F %

options.label: B
options.text: Kelvin (K)

options.label: C
options.text: Degree Celsius C %

options.label: D
options.text: Calorie (cal)

items.answer: (C) Degree Celsius C % The Celsius scale is a common temperature scale, and its unit of temperature is degree Celsius, denoted by the symbol C % .

items.stem: What is the normal temperature of a healthy human body generally taken to be on the Celsius scale? 42 0 %

options.label: D
options.text: C

items.answer: (B) . C 37 0 % The average body temperature of a healthy individual is typically regarded as 37.0°C, although minor deviations may be observed among healthy persons.

items.stem: What is a key difference between clinical thermometers and laboratory thermometers in terms of their use?

options.label: A
options.text: Clinical thermometers use alcohol; laboratory thermometers use mercury

options.label: B
options.text: Clinical thermometers measure air temperature; laboratory thermometers measure body temperature

options.label: C
options.text: Clinical thermometers are for human body temperature; laboratory thermometers are for other purposes

options.label: D
options.text: Laboratory thermometers are digital; clinical thermometers are analog

items.answer: (C) Clinical thermometers are for human body temperature; laboratory thermometers are for other purposes. Clinical thermometers are specifically designed for measuring human body temperatures, while laboratory thermometers are used for a wider range of scientific temperature measurements in experiments.

items.stem: When using a digital clinical thermometer, what should be done immediately before and after use, according to the precautions?

options.label: A
options.text: The thermometer should be shaken vigorously

options.label: B
options.text: The tip of the thermometer should be washed with soap and water

options.label: C
options.text: The battery should be removed and reinserted

options.label: D
options.text: The display should be covered with a cloth

items.answer: (B) The tip of the thermometer should be washed with soap and water. To maintain hygiene and ensure accurate readings, the tip of a digital clinical thermometer must be washed with soap and water both before and after each use.

items.stem: Why might the body temperature of a perfectly healthy person be slightly different from . C 37 0 % ?

options.label: A
options.text: Because thermometers are often inaccurate

options.label: B
options.text: Because . C 37 0% is the maximum normal temperature

options.label: C
options.text: Because normal temperature is an average, and individual variations exist due to factors like age and activity

options.label: D
options.text: Because body temperature only measures illness, not health

items.answer: (C) Because normal temperature is an average, and individual variations exist due to factors like age and activity. The commonly cited . C 37 0 % is an average body temperature for healthy individuals. Actual normal temperatures can vary slightly among people due to factors such as age, time of day, and recent physical activity.

items.stem: What is the equivalent of . C 37 0 % on the Fahrenheit scale? 100 4 %

options.label: D
options.text: F

items.answer: (B) . F 98 6 % A temperature of 37.0°C on the Celsius scale is equivalent to 98.6°F on the Fahrenheit scale.

items.stem: What is the SI unit of temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: Degree Celsius C %

options.label: B
options.text: Degree Fahrenheit F %

options.label: C
options.text: Kelvin (K)

options.label: D
options.text: Joule (J)

items.answer: (C) Kelvin (K) While Celsius and Fahrenheit are commonly used scales, the International System of Units (SI) designates the kelvin (K) as the standard unit for temperature in scientific work.

items.stem: Why is a clinical thermometer NOT suitable for measuring the temperature of boiling water or ice?

options.label: A
options.text: Clinical thermometers are not waterproof

options.label: B
options.text: The temperature range of a clinical thermometer is limited and does not cover these extremes

options.label: C
options.text: Clinical thermometers are only accurate for body temperature

options.label: D
options.text: Boiling water and ice can damage the digital display

items.answer: (B) The temperature range of a clinical thermometer is limited and does not cover these extremes. Clinical thermometers are designed to measure the relatively narrow range of human body temperatures (typically C 35 % . The temperatures of boiling water (around C 100 % ) and ice ( C 0 % ) fall outside this specialized range.

items.stem: What liquid is generally used in the bulb of a common laboratory thermometer, often colored red for visibility?

options.label: A
options.text: Water

options.label: B
options.text: Alcohol

options.label: C
options.text: Mercury

options.label: D
options.text: Glycerine

items.answer: (B) Alcohol Laboratory thermometers typically use either alcohol (often dyed red for visibility) or mercury as the liquid.

items.answer: (C) C 1 % If there is a C 10 % difference between the two bigger marks and this range is divided into 10 smaller divisions, then each small division represents a temperature change of / C C 10 10 1 = % % .

items.stem: When measuring the temperature of warm water with a laboratory thermometer, why should the reading be taken while the thermometer bulb is still immersed in the water?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent the thermometer from breaking

options.label: B
options.text: Because the liquid column might fall quickly once the thermometer is removed from the water

options.label: C
options.text: To ensure the thermometer is held vertically

options.label: D
options.text: Because the glass of the thermometer cools down the water

items.answer: (B) Because the liquid column might fall quickly once the thermometer is removed from the water. Laboratory thermometers (especially those without a kink like clinical ones) show the current temperature of their surroundings. If removed from the warm water, the liquid column will quickly adjust to the cooler air temperature, giving an inaccurate reading of the water’s temperature.

items.stem: What happens to the temperature of water while it is boiling, or the temperature of ice while it is melting, under constant pressure?

options.label: A
options.text: The temperature continuously increases

options.label: B
options.text: The temperature continuously decreases

options.label: C
options.text: The temperature remains constant during the phase change

options.label: D
options.text: The temperature fluctuates rapidly

items.answer: (C) The temperature remains constant during the phase change. During a phase change, such as water boiling into steam or ice melting into water, the temperature of the substance remains constant (e.g., C 100 % for boiling water at sea level, C 0 % for melting ice) until the change is complete.

items.stem: What is a major difference in construction between a typical laboratory thermometer and older mercury clinical thermometers that allows the clinical thermometer to hold its reading after removal from the body? have a wider temperature range.

options.label: A
options.text: Laboratory thermometers have a larger bulb

options.label: B
options.text: Clinical mercury thermometers have a kink or constriction near the bulb

options.label: C
options.text: Laboratory thermometers use alcohol, clinical ones use mercury

options.label: D
options.text: Clinical thermometers

items.answer: (B) Clinical mercury thermometers have a kink or constriction near the bulb. Traditional mercury clinical thermometers have a narrow constriction (kink) in the capillary tube just above the bulb. This kink prevents the mercury from flowing back quickly, allowing the reading to be taken after removing the thermometer. Laboratory thermometers usually lack this feature. (Note: The question specifies older mercury clinical thermometers as digital ones don’t have this kink).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a precaution to be taken while using a laboratory thermometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Handle with care to avoid breakage

options.label: B
options.text: Do not hold it by the bulb

options.label: C
options.text: The bulb should touch the bottom of the beaker for best results

options.label: D
options.text: The thermometer should be held vertically and not tilted

items.answer: (C) The bulb should touch the bottom of the beaker for best results. When measuring liquid temperature, the thermometer bulb should be fully immersed in the liquid but should not touch the bottom or sides of the container, as this might give the temperature of the container rather than the liquid.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : The sense of touch is not always a reliable measure of hotness or coldness. Reason (R) : The sensation of temperature by touch is relative and can be influenced by the previous temperature exposure of the skin.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Our perception of temperature through touch is subjective. As demonstrated in Activity 7.1, an object can feel differently hot or cold depending on whether our hand was previously in contact with something warmer or colder, making it unreliable for precise measurement.

items.stem: The Kelvin scale does not use the degree % sign with its unit K. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

items.answer: (B) 2 and 3 only The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin (K). The unit on the Fahrenheit scale is indeed degree Fahrenheit F % . The Kelvin scale unit (K) is written without a degree symbol. Therefore, statements 2 and 3 are correct.

items.stem: During the COVID-19 pandemic, screeners used non-contact thermometers to measure people’s temperatures from a distance. These thermometers are also known as:

options.label: A
options.text: Mercury thermometers

options.label: B
options.text: Alcohol thermometers

options.label: C
options.text: Infrared thermometers

options.label: D
options.text: Maximum-minimum thermometers

items.answer: (C) Infrared thermometers Non-contact thermometers, often used for quick temperature screening from a distance, typically work by detecting infrared radiation emitted by the body. This reduces physical contact and potential disease transmission.

items.stem: What is the significance of washing the tip of a clinical thermometer with soap and water before and after use?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps the thermometer to read the temperature more quickly

options.label: B
options.text: It prevents the spread of infections and ensures hygiene

options.label: C
options.text: It calibrates the thermometer for accurate readings

options.label: D
options.text: It keeps the digital display clean and clear

items.answer: (B) It prevents the spread of infections and ensures hygiene. Washing the thermometer tip is a crucial hygiene practice to remove any germs or contaminants, thereby preventing the potential spread of infections when the thermometer is used by different individuals or on different body parts.

items.stem: What is the typical temperature range of a laboratory thermometer? 50 - %

options.label: D
options.text: C

items.answer: (C) C 10 - % Laboratory thermometers usually have a temperature range from –10°C to 110°C, making them suitable for a wide range of scientific experiments.

items.stem: When placing a digital thermometer in the armpit for measuring body temperature, how does the reading generally compare to the actual core body temperature? 2 % lower than the core body temperature.

options.label: A
options.text: It is exactly the same as the core body temperature

options.label: B
options.text: It is about . C 0 5 % higher than the core body temperature

options.label: C
options.text: It is about . C 0 5 % lower than the core body temperature

options.label: D
options.text: It is always C

items.answer: (C) It is about . C 0 5 % lower than the core body temperature. The temperature measured in the armpit, known as the axillary temperature, is typically 0.5°C to 1°C lower than the core body temperature.

items.stem: How does the writing convention for the unit Kelvin (K) differ from Celsius C % and Fahrenheit F % ?

options.label: A
options.text: Kelvin uses a lowercase ‘k’, while Celsius and Fahrenheit use uppercase

options.label: B
options.text: The degree sign % is not written with K

options.label: C
options.text: Kelvin is always written with a full stop after it

options.label: D
options.text: Celsius and Fahrenheit do not leave a space between the number and unit

items.answer: (B) The degree sign % is not written with K. While Celsius and Fahrenheit use the degree symbol (e.g., 25°C, 77°F), the kelvin (K) is written without the degree sign for example, 273 K.

items.stem: When using a laboratory thermometer to measure the temperature of a liquid, which of these actions should be AVOIDED?

options.label: A
options.text: Holding the thermometer vertically

options.label: B
options.text: Ensuring the bulb is fully immersed in the liquid

options.label: C
options.text: Allowing the bulb to touch the bottom or sides of the container

options.label: D
options.text: Reading the temperature while the bulb is still in the liquid

items.answer: (C) Allowing the bulb to touch the bottom or sides of the container. The thermometer bulb should measure the liquid’s temperature, not the container’s. Touching the bottom or sides might give an inaccurate reading influenced by the container’s temperature.

items.stem: If a weather report states the maximum air temperature for the day, what does this information primarily indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: The coldest point reached during the day

options.label: B
options.text: The average temperature throughout the day

options.label: C
options.text: The highest temperature the air reached during that day

options.label: D
options.text: The temperature inside buildings

items.answer: (C) The highest temperature the air reached during that day. The maximum air temperature reported in weather forecasts refers to the peak or highest temperature recorded in the air for that specific day and location.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Mercury thermometers are being replaced by digital thermometers. Reason (R) : Mercury is an extremely toxic substance and difficult to dispose of if the thermometer breaks.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. The toxicity of mercury and the environmental hazard it poses upon breakage are significant reasons for the shift towards safer digital thermometers for temperature measurement.

items.stem: It should be held by the tip while taking a reading.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

items.answer: (A) 1 and 2 only Digital clinical thermometers are battery-operated and require contact with the body (e.g., under the tongue) to measure temperature. Holding it by the tip is a precaution to avoid.

items.stem: A student is asked to measure the temperature of melting ice. They have a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer. Which thermometer should they use and why?

options.label: A
options.text: Clinical thermometer, because it is more accurate for low temperatures

options.label: B
options.text: Laboratory thermometer, because its range typically includes C 0% and is designed for such purposes

options.label: C
options.text: Either thermometer, as both will give the same reading

options.label: D
options.text: Clinical thermometer, but only after warming it up

items.answer: (B) Laboratory thermometer, because its range typically includes C 0% and is designed for such purposes. A clinical thermometer’s range (e.g., C 35 % ) does not extend down to C 0 % . A laboratory thermometer, with a typical range like C 10 - % , is appropriate for measuring the temperature of melting ice.

items.stem: What is absolute zero ?

options.label: A
options.text: The boiling point of water on the Kelvin scale

options.label: B
options.text: The lowest possible temperature, close to . C 273 15 - % (0 kelvin)

options.label: C
options.text: The temperature at which mercury freezes

options.label: D
options.text: The normal temperature of the human body in kelvin

items.answer: (B) The lowest possible temperature, close to . C 273 15 - % (0 kelvin). Absolute zero is the theoretical lowest limit of temperature, equivalent to 0 kelvin or approximately . C 273 15 - % . At this temperature, atomic motion would be minimal.

items.stem: If you are reading a laboratory thermometer, why is it important to keep your eye level with the top of the liquid column?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent the liquid from evaporating

options.label: B
options.text: To avoid parallax error and ensure an accurate reading

options.label: C
options.text: To keep the thermometer stable

options.label: D
options.text: To magnify the scale markings

items.answer: (B) To avoid parallax error and ensure an accurate reading. Reading a thermometer scale from an angle (above or below the liquid level) can lead to a parallax error, where the reading appears different from its true value. Eye-level reading minimizes this.

items.stem: The Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales are named in honour of:

options.label: A
options.text: The places where they were first used

options.label: B
options.text: The materials used in the first thermometers

options.label: C
options.text: The scientists who developed these scales

options.label: D
options.text: The phenomena they were designed to measure

items.answer: (C) The scientists who developed these scales. The three common temperature scales Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin are named in honor of the scientists who played key roles in their development.

items.stem: In Activity 7.1, when both hands are placed simultaneously in container B (tap water) after being in warm water

options.label: A
options.text: and ice-cold water (C) respectively, how does the water in B feel to each hand?

options.label: B
options.text: Cold to both hands

options.label: C
options.text: Cold to the hand from A, and warm to the hand from C

options.label: D
options.text: Warm to the hand from A, and cold to the hand from C

items.answer: (C) Cold to the hand from A, and warm to the hand from C. The hand previously in warm water (A) will perceive the tap water (B) as cool. The hand previously in ice-cold water (C) will perceive the same tap water (B) as warm, demonstrating the relativity of touch.

items.stem: Which temperature scale is NOT commonly used in most scientific studies anymore ?

options.label: A
options.text: Celsius scale

options.label: B
options.text: Kelvin scale

options.label: C
options.text: Fahrenheit scale

options.label: D
options.text: None of the above

items.answer: (C) Fahrenheit scale The Fahrenheit scale is no longer commonly used in scientific studies, with Celsius—and especially Kelvin—being the preferred temperature scales in scientific contexts..

items.stem: Which of these is NOT a factor mentioned that can influence normal human body temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: Age

options.label: B
options.text: Time of the day

options.label: C
options.text: Activity level

options.label: D
options.text: Blood type

items.answer: (D) Blood type Factors such as age, time of day, and activity level can cause slight variations in a healthy person’s body temperature, while blood type is not considered one of these influencing factors.

items.stem: What is a reliable measure of the hotness or coldness of a body?
items.answer: A reliable measure of hotness or coldness of a body is its temperature.

items.stem: What is the device used to measure temperature called?
items.answer: A device that measures temperature is called a thermometer.

items.stem: Name the two common types of thermometers.
items.answer: Clinical thermometers and laboratory thermometers.

items.stem: What is the primary use of a clinical thermometer?
items.answer: Clinical thermometers are used to measure human body temperatures.

items.stem: What scale is generally used by clinical thermometers for measuring temperature?
items.answer: Clinical thermometers generally use the Celsius scale.

items.answer: The unit is degree Celsius, denoted by

items.stem: Why are mercury thermometers being replaced by digital thermometers?
items.answer: Mercury is extremely toxic and difficult to dispose of if the thermometer breaks.

items.stem: What type of thermometers were commonly used during the COVID-19 pandemic to measure temperature from a distance?
items.answer: Non-contact thermometers or infrared thermometers were used.

items.stem: What is considered the normal temperature of a healthy human body in degree Celsius?
items.answer: The normal temperature of a healthy human body is taken to be 37.0 ºC.

items.stem: Name one factor that can influence a person’s body temperature.
items.answer: Age (or time of the day, activity level).

items.stem: What is the typical lower limit of temperature that human body temperature normally does not go below?
items.answer: The temperature of human beings does not normally go below 35 ºC.

items.stem: What is the unit of temperature on the Fahrenheit scale and its symbol?
items.answer: The unit is degree Fahrenheit, denoted by °F.

items.stem: What is the SI unit of temperature?
items.answer: The SI unit of temperature is kelvin.

items.stem: What is the symbol for kelvin?
items.answer: The symbol for kelvin is K.

items.stem: What liquid is commonly used in laboratory thermometers, often coloured red?
items.answer: Alcohol is commonly used (or mercury).

items.stem: What is the typical temperature range of a school laboratory thermometer mentioned in the chapter?
items.answer: The range is typically from –10 ºC to 110 ºC.

items.stem: When using a laboratory thermometer to measure water temperature, should the bulb touch the bottom of the beaker?
items.answer: No, the bulb should not touch the bottom or the sides of the beaker.

items.stem: What happens to the temperature of water while it is boiling?
items.answer: The temperature of water remains constant while it is boiling.

items.stem: Who was Anna Mani, also known as the ‘Weather Woman of India’?
items.answer: Anna Mani was an Indian scientist who invented and built many weather measurement instruments.

items.stem: What is the lowest possible temperature called, which is close to −273.15 ºC?
items.answer: It is called absolute zero.

items.stem: Why can we not always rely on our sense of touch to judge if a body is hot or cold?
items.answer: Our sense of touch is subjective and can be misleading, as it depends on the relative temperatures our hands were previously exposed to.

items.stem: What is temperature and how does it relate to the hotness of two bodies?
items.answer: Temperature is a reliable measure of hotness or coldness. A hotter body has a higher temperature than a colder body.

items.stem: What are the main differences in use between a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer?
items.answer: Clinical thermometers are specifically designed to measure human body temperature, while laboratory thermometers are used for various scientific purposes, measuring a wider range of temperatures.

items.stem: Why are digital clinical thermometers preferred over older mercury thermometers?
items.answer: Digital thermometers are preferred because they do not contain toxic mercury, making them safer. Their digital display is also easier to read accurately.

items.stem: What are non-contact thermometers, and why were they particularly useful during the COVID-19 pandemic?
items.answer: Non-contact (infrared) thermometers measure temperature without touching a person’s body. They were useful during the pandemic to reduce the risk of spreading disease.

items.stem: Is the normal body temperature of 37.0 ºC exactly the same for every healthy person? Explain briefly.
items.answer: No, 37.0 ºC is an average. A healthy person’s normal temperature can be slightly different, influenced by age, time of day, and activity.

items.stem: How does the Fahrenheit scale represent normal human body temperature, equivalent to 37.0 ºC?
items.answer: A temperature of 37.0 ºC on the Celsius scale is equivalent to 98.6 ºF on the Fahrenheit scale.

items.stem: How can temperature in Celsius be converted to Kelvin?
items.answer: Temperature in Kelvin scale = Temperature in Celsius scale + 273.15. This is a fundamental conversion in scientific work.

items.stem: Describe the basic structure of a typical laboratory thermometer found in schools.
items.answer: It consists of a long, narrow, uniform sealed glass tube with a bulb at one end containing a liquid (alcohol or mercury) and a Celsius scale marked along the tube.

items.stem: What is meant by the ‘range’ of a laboratory thermometer?
items.answer: The ‘range’ of a laboratory thermometer refers to the lowest and highest temperatures that the thermometer is designed to measure accurately.

items.stem: How do you find the smallest value that a laboratory thermometer can read from its markings?
items.answer: Note the temperature difference between two bigger marks and count the number of smaller divisions between them. Divide the difference by the number of divisions.

items.stem: List two precautions to be taken while handling a laboratory thermometer.
items.answer: Handle it with care to avoid breakage. Do not hold it by the bulb when taking readings, as this can affect accuracy.

items.stem: When measuring the temperature of warm water with a laboratory thermometer, how should it be held and when should the reading be taken?
items.answer: The thermometer should be held vertically, with the bulb fully immersed but not touching the container. The reading must be taken while the thermometer is still immersed.

items.stem: What happens to the reading of a laboratory thermometer if it is taken out of warm water before noting the temperature?
items.answer: If taken out of warm water, the liquid column in a laboratory thermometer begins to fall quickly, so the reading will be inaccurate.

items.stem: What did Anna Mani contribute to the field of weather measurement in India?
items.answer: Anna Mani invented and built a large number of weather measurement instruments, reducing India’s reliance on other nations for such technology.

items.stem: Why are weather reports that include maximum and minimum air temperatures important?
items.answer: These reports are important for daily planning, agriculture and because air temperature data, along with other parameters is used for making weather forecasts.

items.stem: How does the temperature of ice behave while it is melting?
items.answer: The temperature of ice remains constant at its melting point (e.g., 0 ºC at standard pressure) while it is melting.

items.stem: Briefly explain why a clinical thermometer cannot be used to measure the temperature of boiling water.
items.answer: The temperature of boiling water (around 100 ºC) is outside the limited measurement range of a clinical thermometer (typically 35 ºC to 42 ºC).

items.stem: What are the conventions for writing the symbols for degree Celsius, degree Fahrenheit, and kelvin?
items.answer: Symbols are ºC, ºF and K. The degree sign ( º) is used with Celsius and Fahrenheit but not with Kelvin. All symbols are capital letters.

items.stem: Why might the temperature measured in the armpit be slightly lower than the actual body temperature?
items.answer: Temperature measured in the armpit can be about 0.5 ºC to 1 ºC lower because the armpit is an external surface, not reflecting the core body temperature as accurately as an oral reading.

items.stem: Explain why our sense of touch is not a reliable method for determining how hot or cold an object is. Describe a simple activity that demonstrates this.
items.answer: Our sense of touch is relative and can be easily fooled. For example, if you place one hand in warm water and the other in cold water, then place both in lukewarm water, the first hand will feel the lukewarm water as cold, and the second will feel it as warm. This shows its unavailability.

items.stem: What is a clinical thermometer? Describe the features of a modern digital clinical thermometer and list two precautions for its correct use.
items.answer: A clinical thermometer is used to measure human body temperature. Modern digital ones display temperature numerically, run on batteries, and use heat sensors. Precautions: Wash the tip with soap and water before and after use, and read the instruction manual for proper operation and placement (e.g., under the tongue).

items.stem: What are the Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin scales of temperature? Mention the SI unit of temperature and explain its significance.
items.answer: Celsius (ºC) and Fahrenheit (ºF) are common temperature scales, with Celsius used widely in science. Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature, crucial in scientific work because it starts from absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature. Temperatures are converted for different applications.

items.stem: Describe the correct procedure for measuring the temperature of warm water using a laboratory thermometer, highlighting at least three key steps for accuracy.
items.answer: 1. Hold the thermometer vertically, immersing the bulb completely in the warm water without it touching the container’s bottom or sides.

items.stem: Why was mercury commonly used in older thermometers, and what are the significant disadvantages that led to its replacement by digital alternatives?
items.answer: Mercury was used because it expands uniformly with temperature and is easily visible. However, mercury is highly toxic. If a mercury thermometer breaks, the spilled mercury poses a serious health and environmental hazard, making its disposal difficult. Digital thermometers avoid this risk.

items.stem: Explain how a non-contact infrared thermometer works and why it became a preferred tool in public health scenarios like pandemics.
items.answer: Non-contact infrared thermometers measure the infrared radiation emitted by a person’s body (usually the forehead) to determine temperature without physical contact. This reduces the risk of cross-contamination and disease transmission, making them ideal for quick, safe screening in public health emergencies.

items.stem: What is meant by the ‘range’ and ‘smallest readable value’ (or least count) of a laboratory thermometer? Why is it important to know these before using one?
items.answer: The ‘range’ is the interval between the lowest and highest temperatures the thermometer can measure. The ‘smallest readable value’ is the smallest temperature change it can detect, indicated by its smallest division. Knowing these ensures the thermometer is suitable for the expected temperature and read accurately.

items.stem: Who was Anna Mani and what was her significant contribution to India in the field of meteorology? Why is accurate weather measurement important?
items.answer: Anna Mani was an Indian physicist and meteorologist known as the Weather Woman of India. She designed and standardized numerous weather instruments, reducing India’s dependence on imports. Accurate weather measurement is vital for forecasting, agriculture, disaster management, and understanding climate change.

items.stem: Phi ban wants to measure the temperature of tap water and then the temperature of boiling water for a science experiment. She has a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer. (i) Which thermometer should Phi ban use to measure the temperature of tap water? Why? (ii) Can Phi ban use the clinical thermometer to measure the temperature of boiling water? Explain your answer. (Evaluating) (iii) If the laboratory thermometer reads 25 ºC for tap water, what precautions should she take while measuring?
items.answer: (i) Phi ban should use the laboratory thermometer. Tap water temperature is likely within its range, and clinical thermometers are for body temperature only. (ii) No, Phi ban cannot use the clinical thermometer for boiling water. Boiling water (around 100 ºC) is far above the maximum temperature range of a clinical thermometer (around 42 ºC). (iii) She should ensure the bulb is immersed in water, not touching the container, hold it vertically, and read the scale at eye level while immersed.

items.stem: A weather report states that the maximum temperature for the day in Delhi was 40 ºC and the minimum was 28 ºC. Lam bok wonders how these temperatures are measured. (i) What kind of thermometer is likely used at weather stations to measure air temperature? (ii) Why does the air temperature vary between maximum and minimum in a single day? (iii) How is this air temperature data useful beyond just knowing if it’s hot or cold?
items.answer: (i) Weather stations use specialized thermometers, often maximum-minimum thermometers or electronic sensors, designed for measuring air temperatures accurately. (ii) Air temperature varies due to the Earth’s rotation, leading to changes in the amount of solar radiation received at different times of the day. (iii) This data is crucial for weather forecasting, agricultural planning, understanding climate patterns, and public health advisories during extreme weather.

items.stem: A digital clinical thermometer shows a reading of 98.6 ºF for a healthy person. Another healthy person’s temperature is measured as 37.2 ºC using a different digital clinical thermometer. (i) Are these two temperatures significantly different in indicating health status? (ii) What is the SI unit of temperature, and is it commonly displayed on clinical thermometers? (iii) If a child’s temperature is taken in the armpit and reads 37.5 ºC, what might be closer to their actual core body temperature?
items.answer: (i) No, 98.6 ºF is equivalent to 37.0 ºC. A reading of 37.2 ºC is very close and within the normal healthy range. (ii) The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin (K). It is not commonly displayed on clinical thermometers, which usually show Celsius or Fahrenheit. (iii) The actual core body temperature might be closer to 38.0 ºC or 38.5 ºC, as armpit readings are typically 0.5 ºC to 1 ºC lower.

items.stem: In a school laboratory, students are asked to find the smallest temperature value a given laboratory thermometer can measure. The marks 20 º C and 30 ºC are visible, with 10 small divisions between them. (i) What is the temperature difference between the two bigger marks (20 ºC and 30 ºC)? (ii) How much temperature does one small division on this thermometer indicate? (iii) What is the smallest value this thermometer can accurately read?
items.answer: (i) The temperature difference is 30 ºC – 20 ºC = 10 ºC. (ii) One small division indicates 10 ºC ÷ 10 divisions = 1 ºC. (iii) The smallest value this thermometer can accurately read is 1 ºC.

items.stem: Lambok read that the core of the Sun has a temperature of about 15 million degrees Celsius, while absolute zero is – 273.15 ºC. He wonders if these temperatures can be measured by ordinary thermometers. (i) Can a laboratory thermometer measure the Sun’s core temperature? Why or why not? (Evaluating) (ii) What does absolute zero represent in terms of temperature? (iii) Which temperature scale has its zero point at absolute zero?
items.answer: (i) No, a laboratory thermometer cannot measure the Sun’s core temperature. Its range is extremely limited compared to such high temperatures, and it would vaporize instantly. (ii) Absolute zero (0 Kelvin or −273.15 ºC) is the lowest possible temperature, where theoretically, all molecular motion ceases. (iii) The Kelvin scale has its zero point at absolute zero.
